holidays.name: National Cherry Cobbler Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the warm, bubbly, buttery dessert of baked cherries topped with a golden biscuit or cake-like crust. Bonus points if you eat it with a scoop of vanilla ice cream melting on top.
holidays.origin: Like many American food observances, it grew out of food-fan and dessert-lover circles and spread through calendars of unofficial food days. No single official founder is clearly documented.
holidays.funFact: Cobblers are thought to be named for their 'cobbled' look, since the biscuit topping resembles a rough cobblestone street.

holidays.name: International Day Against Homophobia, Transphobia and Biphobia (IDAHOBIT)
holidays.description: A global awareness day that draws attention to discrimination and violence against LGBTQ+ people. Events include flag raisings, art displays, and community gatherings around the world.
holidays.origin: It was first celebrated in 2005 and commemorates May 17, 1990, when the World Health Organization removed homosexuality from its International Classification of Diseases.
holidays.funFact: It is observed in over 130 countries, and in some places the day is marked by large public events such as rainbow flag displays on government buildings.

holidays.name: World Telecommunication and Information Society Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to celebrating how phones, the internet, and other communication technologies connect the world, and a handy reminder to call your relatives instead of just texting them.
holidays.origin: It marks the founding of the International Telegraph Union on May 17, 1865, and has been celebrated annually since 1969. The UN General Assembly expanded it in 2006 to include the information society.
holidays.funFact: The International Telecommunication Union is one of the oldest international organizations still in existence, older than the United Nations by 80 years.

holidays.name: Norwegian Constitution Day (Syttende Mai)
holidays.description: Norway's national day is a gigantic party with children's parades, brass bands, traditional bunad costumes, and an astonishing quantity of hot dogs and ice cream. It is famous for being more about kids waving flags than military might.
holidays.origin: It commemorates the signing of the Norwegian Constitution at Eidsvoll on May 17, 1814, which declared Norway an independent nation.
holidays.funFact: Norwegians often greet each other with 'Gratulerer med dagen!' and the biggest parade in Oslo passes by the Royal Palace, where the royal family waves from the balcony for hours.

holidays.name: National Walnut Day (Observed Mid-May)
holidays.description: Nutty lovers rejoice! A day to crack open a few walnuts, bake them into brownies, or just toss them on a salad and feel fancy.
holidays.origin: Unofficial food-day calendars list it in mid-May, and the date is celebrated by nut enthusiasts and walnut growers. The origin is loosely tied to the walnut industry's promotion efforts.
holidays.funFact: Walnuts are one of the oldest tree foods known to humans, with evidence of consumption dating back to around 7000 BC.
